article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-dominant hybrid
Genetics: A parallel line to Super Silver Haze
Breeder: Mr. Nice Seedbank
THC Content: 17–22%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: myrcene , terpinolene, beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Ripe mango, tropical fruit, pineapple, citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–11 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: 450–550 grams per square meter
Outdoor Yield: Potentially very high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate to advanced

Mango Haze comes from an era when cannabis breeding was driven less by extreme THC percentages and more by the search for exceptional combinations of aroma, structure, resin, and character. Created by Nevil Schoenmakers and Shantibaba for Mr. Nice Seedbank, this old-school sativa hybrid blends Northern Lights #5 , Skunk , and Haze genetics into flower capable of producing an uncannily ripe tropical-fruit aroma.

Mr. Nice describes the cultivar as 25% NL5, 25% Skunk, and 50% Haze, with the same Haze father used in Super Silver Haze and a mother selected from the same family. The result is marijuana that smells of fully ripened mango layered with citrus, spice, herbs, and incense rather than the syrupy candy notes of newer fruit strains. Its cerebral high can feel expansive, creative, and dreamlike, while enough Northern Lights and Skunk influence remains to provide body and structure without eliminating the classic Haze personality.
Genetics and Lineage

Mango Haze shares one of the most distinguished family trees in European cannabis breeding. Mr. Nice Seedbank explains that the cultivar is a parallel line to Super Silver Haze: both share the same Haze father, while Mango Haze’s mother is a sister to the mother used for Super Silver Haze. The resulting genetic composition is 50% Haze, 25% Northern Lights #5, and 25% Skunk. Mr. Nice credits Nevil and Shantibaba as the breeders. That relationship explains why Mango Haze can display many of the desirable characteristics associated with Super Silver Haze while developing a noticeably fruitier aromatic direction.

Haze provides the dominant personality. Its influence appears in the elongated growth, cerebral effects, spicy-incense background, and tendency for certain phenotypes to require a longer flowering period. Northern Lights #5 helps moderate that architecture by introducing heavier resin production and physical depth, while Skunk adds vigor, yield, pungency, and additional fruit character. Instead of one parent completely taking control, different plants can emphasize different parts of the ancestry. One expression may lean intensely toward tropical mango and finish comparatively quickly, while another can show more traditional Haze structure and require considerably longer before reaching full maturity.

That variation is part of the appeal of the original seed line. Mango Haze was not designed as a highly uniform modern commercial clone where every plant looks and smells nearly identical. Phenotype hunting can reveal differences in flowering time, structure, resin, and aroma, making the cultivar particularly interesting to experienced growers looking for a keeper rather than simply predictable production.
Effects and Experience

Mango Haze is predominantly cerebral cannabis. The experience usually begins with a noticeable increase in mental activity and sensory interest rather than a heavy wave of physical relaxation. Ideas can move freely, conversation becomes more engaging, and music or visual surroundings may feel unusually detailed. Mr. Nice describes the high as strong and dreamlike, with pronounced creativity and introspective potential. Unlike some modern high-THC hybrids that overwhelm quickly, a well-selected Mango Haze phenotype can develop in layers, gradually becoming more immersive while preserving a relatively clear mental quality.

The Haze component is balanced by enough Northern Lights and Skunk influence to give the experience some grounding. After the initial cerebral rise, a mild physical ease may become noticeable without necessarily turning into sedation. Moderate servings can fit daytime recreation, creative work, social settings, outdoor activities, or music particularly well for experienced cannabis consumers. Larger doses may become much more introspective and spacey, potentially making complicated tasks difficult despite the absence of traditional couch-lock.

Consumers sensitive to stimulating weed should approach the cultivar carefully. Too much can produce racing thoughts, restlessness, dry mouth, dizziness, or anxiety, especially with strongly Haze-dominant phenotypes. THC levels also vary widely between plants, so a familiar strain name should never substitute for knowing the potency of the actual batch.
Medical Benefits

The energetic and mentally engaging nature of Mango Haze may interest medical marijuana consumers who prefer avoiding heavily sedating cannabis during the day. Some patients choose sativa-dominant cultivars when temporary fatigue, low motivation, reduced appetite, stress, or physical discomfort interferes with ordinary activity. The relatively light body component may also appeal to people who want cannabis effects without immediately feeling sleepy or physically slowed.

Mango Haze itself has not been clinically proven to treat depression, anxiety, pain, ADHD, or another specific condition. Its terpene chemistry also varies significantly between phenotypes. Myrcene is often prominent in mango-forward expressions, while terpinolene, pinene, caryophyllene, limonene, and linalool can contribute varying degrees of herbs, spice, citrus, pine, flowers, and fruit. Consumers using marijuana medically should rely on batch-specific laboratory testing whenever possible.

The original cultivar should also not be confused with CBD Mango Haze. Mr. Nice offers that as a separate CBD-rich breeding project, with average CBD around 8–10% and THC around 6–8%. Classic Mango Haze is the THC-oriented old-school version described on this page.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Ripe mango is not merely a convenient name for this cultivar; exceptional phenotypes can smell remarkably close to the actual fruit. Mr. Nice specifically highlights the aroma of fully ripe mangos as one of the plant’s defining qualities. When well cured, the flower can release sweet tropical fruit first, followed by pineapple, orange or lemon peel, herbs, pepper, and the dry incense-like character associated with classic Haze.

The flavor develops with similar complexity. Mango and tropical sweetness lead the inhale, but the finish becomes less sugary as spice, wood, herbs, and faint Skunk pungency move forward. Haze-dominant plants may carry more incense and pepper, while fruit-selected expressions can remain juicy and tropical through most of the exhale. Pinene-rich plants can introduce a sharper green quality, whereas myrcene can deepen the ripe-fruit and earthy side.

This profile makes Mango Haze quite different from newer marijuana strains that achieve fruit flavor through candy, Gelato, or dessert genetics. The sweetness here sits on top of an unmistakably old-school Haze foundation, giving the cultivar both tropical accessibility and considerably more aromatic depth.
Growing Information

Mr. Nice lists an indoor flowering period of approximately eight to eleven weeks, with finishing time depending heavily on the mother and phenotype selected. Indoor plants can yield approximately 450–550 grams per square meter under suitable lighting, and experienced growers may exceed those figures. Height is the first major consideration. Even when flowering begins from a rooted clone or young seed plant, the breeder notes that Mango Haze can still reach roughly one to one-and-a-half meters.

Growers with limited vertical space should therefore control the plant early. Topping, low-stress training, supercropping, and selective removal of lower branches can help redirect growth into a manageable canopy. Mr. Nice specifically recommends pruning lower branches so energy concentrates in the primary cola clusters. A screen can also be useful for turning the cultivar’s Haze stretch into a broad productive surface rather than allowing individual branches to rise beyond the ideal lighting zone.

One favorable characteristic is its resistance to mold, something the breeder highlights for both indoor and outdoor cultivation. Outdoors, however, the longer phenotypes require a sufficiently warm climate to finish properly. Mr. Nice notes that Northern Hemisphere plants are best suited to southern European-style regions such as Spain, Italy, and southern France, where they can mature during October. Growers in colder areas may have more success in a greenhouse. Harvest should ultimately be determined by trichome maturity and flower development rather than a predetermined date.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Mango Haze?

Mango Haze is approximately 25% Northern Lights #5, 25% Skunk, and 50% Haze. Mr. Nice Seedbank describes it as a parallel breeding line to Super Silver Haze, sharing the same Haze father while using a sister of the SSH mother.
Who bred Mango Haze?
The original Mango Haze was created by Nevil Schoenmakers and Shantibaba and released through Mr. Nice Seedbank. The breeder continues to list it among its classic old-school genetics.
Is Mango Haze indica or sativa?

Mango Haze is a sativa-dominant hybrid. Half of its genetic makeup comes from Haze, while Northern Lights #5 and Skunk make up approximately 25% each. Its cerebral effects and stretching growth pattern strongly reflect the Haze side.
Is Mango Haze the same as CBD Mango Haze?

No. Original Mango Haze and CBD Mango Haze are separate cultivars. CBD Mango Haze was developed later as a CBD-rich version and typically produces much more CBD and substantially less THC than the original.
How long does Mango Haze take to flower?

Mr. Nice gives an indoor flowering period of approximately eight to eleven weeks. Faster phenotypes can finish near the beginning of that range, while stronger Haze expressions may require considerably more time.
Final Thoughts on Mango Haze

Mango Haze represents a different philosophy of cannabis breeding from the one dominating today’s dispensary shelves. Nevil and Shantibaba combined Northern Lights #5, Skunk, and Haze genetics to produce marijuana valued not simply for THC but for cerebral character, resin, yield, phenotype diversity, and an extraordinary ripe-mango aroma. Its relationship to Super Silver Haze gives it genuine historical significance, while the tropical flavor allows the cultivar to remain accessible even to consumers who normally find classic Haze weed too spicy or incense-heavy.

For growers, Mango Haze requires more attention than a compact eight-week commercial hybrid. Stretch, phenotype variation, and potentially long flowering times reward planning and experience, although mold resistance and 450–550 gram-per-square-meter indoor yields make the effort worthwhile. For consumers, the reward is an increasingly uncommon type of high: bright, creative, introspective, and unmistakably Haze-driven, wrapped in ripe mango, tropical fruit, herbs, citrus, and spice. More than two decades after its creation, Mango Haze remains an excellent example of why carefully preserved old-school cannabis genetics still have something modern hybrids cannot easily reproduce.
